name: Verrucous Hemangioma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Verrucous Hemangioma

criteria.description: Presence of congenital or early childhood verrucous, hyperkeratotic, bluish-red vascular lesion typically on lower extremities
Histological evidence of proliferation of dilated, thin-walled vascular channels extending into deep dermis and subcutaneous tissue with overlying epidermal hyperplasia and hyperkeratosis
MRI or ultrasound showing vascular lesion with deep tissue involvement without bone invasion

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical lesion with confirmatory histopathology showing deep dermal and subcutaneous vascular proliferation with epidermal changes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Differentiation from other vascular malformations and tumors is critical due to treatment implications

imaging: MRI showing deep dermal and subcutaneous vascular lesion without bone involvement
other: Histopathology revealing dilated vascular channels with overlying epidermal hyperplasia and hyperkeratosis

distinguishingFeatures: Superficial vascular lesion limited to papillary dermis
Lack of deep dermal and subcutaneous involvement
Smaller lesion size and less progressive growth
Presence of spindle cell proliferation on histology

redFlags: Rapid lesion growth suggesting malignant transformation
Persistent bleeding refractory to local measures
references: Enzinger and Weiss's Soft Tissue Tumors, 6th Edition
